mission: AI can now write software far faster than humans can check it. Safeguarded AI funds an open-source toolkit that lets fleets of AI agents produce formally verified (mathematically proven) code, control systems and models, with quantitative guarantees of correctness and fail-safety, and demonstrates it on real cybersecurity problems.

key_work.title: Safeguarded AI programme thesis (updated May 2026)
key_work.plain_summary: Updated plan: broaden the TA1 tooling into an open mathematical assurance toolkit and apply it first to high-impact cybersecurity challenges.

status_note: launched 2024 by the UK's Advanced Research + Invention Agency with £59m. Nov 2025–May 2026 it narrowed focus: dropped the planned TA2 and TA3 Phase 2 cyber-physical calls, expanded the TA1 'mathematical assurance toolkit', and shifted to cybersecurity applications. In April 2026 founding director David 'davidad' Dalrymple became Technical Advisor and Nora Ammann became Programme Director.

warnings.text: Our ability to verify software has not kept up with AI's ability to write it.
High-risk dual-use AI capabilities are becoming openly available faster than expected.
Deploying AI in critical systems without guarantees requires costly human-in-the-loop oversight or risks failures.

recommendations.text: Give AI-produced code and control systems machine-checked, quantitative guarantees of correctness and fail-safety.
Build open, usable formal-verification infrastructure that AI agents can operate at scale.
Apply provable security first where the need is most urgent: cybersecurity.
